currentPancakePolicies.label: pancakeswap-v3 exactInput
warnings: Static exact-chain/address ABI and source inventory only; no grant, fresh runtime identity, persistent implementation, liquidity, funding, financial-safety or execution guarantee. Canonical calldata/value checks, exact grants, pauses and independent policies remain mandatory.

Caller selects assets, amounts, route, fee tiers, price limits and recipient. Existing token allowance/balance and pool liquidity are required; no permit, approval, role, callback entrypoint, multicall, position-manager or settlement-helper capability is added.

All selected swaps are payable. pay wraps the constructor-bound WETH9/native wrapper only when the input token equals that wrapper and the router has enough native balance, otherwise it pulls approved caller ERC20 or uses router-held intermediate tokens. Native asset is chain-specific, not necessarily ETH; wrapped-native output remains ERC20 and is not automatically unwrapped.

Prefer approved ERC20 input with zero native value. Overpayment and partial fills can leave native or token dust in the router; swaps do not automatically refund it, public refund/sweep/unwrap helpers are excluded, and publicly callable contract helpers make router-custodied balances unsafe. Do not assume dust is reserved for this caller.
Original/Pancake tuples retain deadline and check block.timestamp against it. A zero recipient redirects output into router custody, not to the caller; use the intended nonzero token recipient.

Pancake pools are deterministically derived from immutable deployer plus token pair, fee and source-fixed pool init-code hash, not a caller target. pancakeV3SwapCallback authenticates msg.sender against that derived pool before payment.

Packed path bytes encode token addresses and uint24 fee tiers only, not arbitrary calldata. exactInput follows forward token order; exactOutput requires reversed token/fee order and recurses only through authenticated pool callbacks. Malformed paths, unsupported fees or absent pools revert.
Exact-input multihop checks final amountOutMinimum; intermediate outputs are held and paid by the router. Rounding, liquidity gaps, token behavior and price movement can affect execution.

reviewBasis.lifecyclePolicy: scripts/defi-catalog/README.md lifecycle exclusion applies: retired/deprecated/unmaintained deployments are unsupported even exit-only. Current official documentation still lists all15 reviewed targets without retirement marking; Monad official mainnet launch announcement independently corroborates mainnet product attribution. This does not prove live funding or execution.
reviewBasis.priorDispositionChange: Previous router-swap-capability-completion limited Pancake fixed V3 router to swaps and excluded public payment helpers only as outside ordinary-swap scope. This assignment expressly includes additional source-bound direct financial methods, so five decoded concrete settlement helpers are reviewed/admitted with whole-balance custody/fee/native risks, not opaque multicall or authority acquisition. Existing BSC NPM bounded multicall is preserved unchanged and not copied to new chains.
reviewBasis.identityDeduplication: Compared against freshly loaded current catalog using exact chainId + lowercase target address + full canonical signature. Existing27 Pancake entries are preserved without duplicates; no profiles or grants expand.
reviewBasis.bindingLimitations: Sourcify match labels are retained, including Base NPM runtime-only match with no creation match and Dackie-renamed matching source metadata. Monad uses each own exact-address MonadScan Exact Match document after Sourcify404. No BSC ABI or same-address ABI is cloned to another chain; identical fragments are independently extracted from each target provider response. No fresh runtime RPC attestation is claimed.

pragma solidity >=0.6.0 <0.8.0;

/**
 * @dev Interface of the ERC20 Permit extension allowing approvals to be made via signatures, as defined in
 * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612[EIP-2612].
 *
 * Adds the {permit} method, which can be used to change an account's ERC20 allowance (see {IERC20-allowance}) by
 * presenting a message signed by the account. By not relying on `{IERC20-approve}`, the token holder account doesn't
 * need to send a transaction, and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
 */
interface IERC20Permit {
    /**
     * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over `owner`'s tokens,
     * given `owner`'s signed approval.
     *
     * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
     * ordering also apply here.
     *
     * Emits an {Approval} event.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
     * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
     * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
     * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
     * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
     * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
     *
     * For more information on the signature format, see the
     * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
     * section].
     */
    function permit(address owner, address spender, uint256 value, uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) external;

    /**
     * @dev Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be
     * included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}.
     *
     * Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This
     * prevents a signature from being used multiple times.
     */
    function nonces(address owner) external view returns (uint256);

    /**

warnings: Source/ABI admission is not current deployed bytecode, configuration, ownership, funding, balance, liquidity, price, execution-success or financial-safety attestation. Caller selects assets, amounts, route, fee tiers, price limits and recipient. Existing token allowance/balance and pool liquidity are required; no permit, approval, role, callback entrypoint, multicall, position-manager or settlement-helper capability is added.

All selected swaps are payable. pay wraps the constructor-bound WETH9/native wrapper only when the input token equals that wrapper and the router has enough native balance, otherwise it pulls approved caller ERC20 or uses router-held intermediate tokens. Native asset is chain-specific, not necessarily ETH; wrapped-native output remains ERC20 and is not automatically unwrapped.

Prefer approved ERC20 input with zero native value. Overpayment and partial fills can leave native or token dust in the router; swaps do not automatically refund it. Independently granted public refund/sweep/unwrap helpers are separate calls, and router-custodied balances are publicly recoverable rather than reserved for this caller. Avoid stranded funds.
Original/Pancake tuples retain deadline and check block.timestamp against it. A zero recipient redirects output into router custody, not to the caller; use the intended nonzero token recipient.

Pancake pools are deterministically derived from immutable deployer plus token pair, fee and source-fixed pool init-code hash, not a caller target. pancakeV3SwapCallback authenticates msg.sender against that derived pool before payment.

Packed path bytes encode token addresses and uint24 fee tiers only, not arbitrary calldata. exactInput follows forward token order; exactOutput requires reversed token/fee order and recurses only through authenticated pool callbacks. Malformed paths, unsupported fees or absent pools revert.
Exact-input multihop checks final amountOutMinimum; intermediate outputs are held and paid by the router. Rounding, liquidity gaps, token behavior and price movement can affect execution.
